title: Bound S4 spectator workspace by inversion slack
body:
A normalized S4 word with `m` simple rank-one paid calls, active endpoint width `w`, and ordered-pair crossing rank `L` now has a constructive restriction to at most **`w + m - L` total roles**. One spectator-only scalar basis change fixes the original active coordinates and preserves every paid label, order, idempotent, and the entire formal endpoint for arbitrary dirty inputs.

This resolves a positive-slack successor to the zero-slack spectator lemma in [PR4765](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4765), exact merged head `62ae3a67d931f73cb7980e69b8185b44c2679241`. The new proof establishes the local image/functional charge, constructs nested spectator splits, and proves the global full-group-algebra intertwiners. A sharpness example applies only to the stated fixed-basis, factor-preserving reduction: its cancellable pair does not give an optimal-workspace lower bound for the endpoint.

The contribution is contained in `research/s4-slack-workspace-bound/`. It supplies a written quantified proof and finite implementation controls, with no fixed-target census or new κ/native supplier claim. Sources and predecessor credits are pinned in `SOURCES.json`; all are provenance rather than runtime inputs. [Canonical investigation and claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2570#discussioncomment-19131478).

Validation completed locally:

- Registered Python 3.12 replay and direct isolated optimized primary replay: 2,419,200 exact local peel controls, 341 constructive splits, eight full formal fixtures.
- Separate literal regular-action implementation: 4,968 per-factor columns and 1,440 whole-word columns, including all dirty and discarded inputs; it imports no primary verifier.
- Seven semantic boundary groups and eight actual optimized-CLI receipt mutations reject invalid evidence.
- Selected baseline bindings passed; that check is not a selected-construction replay. Commit-byte/source-history preflight and committed Git-free export results are recorded below.

The proof received separate coordinating Codex review. Both implementations were prepared in this session with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; no independent human or formal-kernel acceptance is claimed. No C++, Lean, Docker, historical heavy replay, or hosted-CI result is asserted.
